Word 1: **frustrate**

> From Photo 1: derived forms — *frustrating*, *frustrated*

Meaning: make someone feel stuck or upset because they can’t do what they want.

Close the book — type the spelling (**frus-trate**), then one short sentence. Go!
I am frustrated with my cat

Nice — **frustrated** shows you get the feeling: stuck or upset (even with a cat!). That’s the word family of **frustrate**.

Quick spelling lock: type just the base word **frustrate** once (f-r-u-s-t-r-a-t-e). Then we’ll do **fulfil**.
frustrate

Yes — **frustrate** is locked!

Word 2: **fulfil** (British spelling — one **l** at the end)

> From Photo 1: *to fulfil a dream*

Meaning: make a wish or plan come true; finish what you set out to do.

Close the book — type **fulfil**, then one short sentence (dream, goal, or promise). Go!

Word **7**: **fundraising**

> From Photo 1: **fundraising** — raising money for a cause (like a school or charity)

Close the book. Type the spelling (**fund-rais-ing**), then one short sentence about collecting money for something. Go!
fundraising Fundraising is a good way to donate money to poor people

Yes — **fundraising** is locked! Your sentence shows you get it: collecting money to help people. Nice.

Word **8**: **fussy**

> From Photo 1: **fussy** — hard to please; picky about small things

Close the book. Type **fussy**, then one short sentence (food, clothes, or a picky person). Go!
fussy don't be to fussy to others

Yes — **fussy** is locked! Your meaning is right: don’t be picky or hard to please with people.

Tiny spelling tip: use **too** (t-o-o) when you mean “more than enough” — *don’t be **too** fussy*.

Word **9**: **gauge**

> From Photo 1: **gauge** — a that measures something (like a *rain gauge*)

Close the book. Type **gauge** (that quiet **u**!), then one short sentence. Go!
gauge is a tool to measure things I m

Yes — **gauge** is locked! You kept that quiet **u**, and your meaning is spot on: a that measures.

(Looks like your sentence got cut off at “I m” — that’s okay; the idea is clear.)

Word **10**: **generous**

> From Photo 2: **generous** — happy to give or share; not stingy (antonym: *mean*)

Close the book. Type **generous**, then one short sentence. Go!
g

Good start — **g**… You’re on the right track!

Try chunking it: **gen** – **er** – **ous** (sounds like “jen-uh-rus”).

Type the whole word **generous**, then one short sentence about sharing or giving. You’ve got this!
genruos

So close, Ryan! You got **gen**… and you had almost all the letters.

The order is: **gen** – **er** – **ous** → **generous**  
(Say it: *jen-uh-rus* — there’s an **e** after **n**, then **rous**.)

Type **generous** once more, then one short sentence about sharing. Go!
generous Be generous with your friends

Yes — **generous** is locked! That was a tough spelling and you stuck with it. Great sentence too — sharing with friends is exactly what **generous** means.

Word **11**: **genuine**

> From Photo 2: **genuine** — real or true; not fake

Close the book. Type **genuine**, then one short sentence. Go!
genuun

Almost! You started right with **gen**…

It’s **gen** – **u** – **ine** → **genuine**  
(Say it: *jen-yoo-in* — ends with **ine**, not double **u**.)

Type **genuine** once more, then one short sentence about something real. Go!
genuin

So close — just one letter short!

It’s **genuine** — add the **e** at the end (**genuin** + **e**).

Type **genuine**, then one short sentence about something real. You’ve almost got it!
genuine is that gold genuine

Yes — **genuine** is locked! You kept trying until that final **e** landed. And your sentence nails it: real gold, not fake.

Last numbered word — **12**: **gesture**

> From Photo 2: **gesture** — a hand sign or body movement that shows a feeling or idea

Close the book. Type **gesture**, then one short sentence. Go!
gesture some people use hand gesture to comuinicat

Yes — **gesture** is locked! Your meaning is perfect: hands that help people talk. (Tiny tip later: *communicate* — but **gesture** is what we needed.)

**Batch done — words 7 to 12!** Nice work sticking with the hard spellings (*generous*, *genuine*).
